correctness.rationale: Exact graph Laplacian projector weights yield a diagonal M-matrix resolvent with one quadratic crossing per part. An explicit comparison identity isolates the smallest part; a differentiated radical gives 0<F′≤σ/2 and F′>0, allowing the strict edge-deficit argument for every integer multipartition. Exact Gaussian elimination independently checks representative finite cases. Finite tests are not substituted for the universal analytic proof.

value.rationale: For a fixed count of unit-mass vertices and sum of installed conductances, the exact timestep-preserving nonnegativity frontier is a natural mesh and network-design invariant. The complete strict optimum across all multipartitions depends on the smallest prime factor of the vertex count, a nonobvious arithmetic selection rule with explicit all-order formula; it is not merely a tabulated low-order instance or an unmotivated special invariant. The objective is nonnegativity, not convergence error or mixing speed.
